source.title: Dynamic Momentum Recalibration in Online Gradient Learning
source.authors: Zhi-Peng Yao; Rui-Long Yu; Gui-Song Chang; Ying Li; Yu Zhang; Dazhou Li

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendix text supplied; some tables and figures are flattened, but relevant numerical table entries are legible.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures train and test accuracy for optimizer comparisons and explicitly reports generalization-gap differences, a conceptual test of V4. It does not test memorization of random labels, width beyond interpolation, architecture bias as defined by V3, batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.gate_note: Optimizer comparisons and the explicit train/test gap statement in Appendix E.1 bear on V4. Hessian and gradient-distribution measurements are reported as optimizer analyses, but do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance. Other benchmark results compare optimizer performance without reporting a claim-relevant training/test gap; they are not separate rows here. Cited findings are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: Table 9 directly compares adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD on held-out image-classification accuracy, bearing on V4 without requiring an explicit train/test gap. However, R1–R6 record SGDF's own performance rather than the adaptive-versus-SGD comparison. Tuning also extends beyond learning rates and schedules to momentum coefficients and some weight-decay settings.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they argue that dynamic filtering balances gradient bias and variance and improves the convergence–generalization tradeoff. This is their interpretation; the results do not establish universal superiority, and Adam has better WGAN-GP FID than SGDF.
record.recipe_differences: This study proposes and evaluates SGDF, a dynamic filter-based optimizer, rather than reproducing the optimizer comparisons in the version's cited studies. It also compares multiple optimizers under its own search and training settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports optimizer outcomes across architectures and datasets; it states that SGDF's gain when integrated into Adam differs by architecture, with a larger improvement for VGG11 than for ResNet34 or DenseNet121.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors collectively report that SGDF achieves higher CIFAR test accuracy and smaller train/test accuracy gaps than competing optimizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dynamic filtering of momentum gradients can improve held-out performance and reduce generalization gaps in the tested CNN training recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: AdamW has Hessian trace 0.39 and maximum eigenvalue 0.11, yet the authors report approximately four percentage points lower test accuracy than other methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled Hessian flatness need not rank held-out accuracy across optimizers with different weight-decay formulations.

record.problems: For the relevant explicit train/test gap result, the paper gives only a qualitative collective statement and no numerical gap values. Results are averaged over three seeds; the text says confidence intervals ([µ ± σ]) are shown in figures.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were left out. The paper reports other optimizer metric comparisons, but they do not measure the claim versions' named phenomena or an explicit train/test gap, so they were not included as rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-versus-random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.

A controlled comparison of limited versus broader tuning; optimizer switching; a controlled decoupled-weight-decay recovery experiment. The supplied flattened language-model curves do not establish Adam's ordering relative to SGD. Equal or better adaptive training performance cannot be verified from the flattened CIFAR curves.
Controlled batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout and joint dropout/weight-decay removal ablations.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its ranking of generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.

missing.what: Replace the claim-irrelevant gap rows with adaptive-versus-momentum-SGD test-accuracy comparisons. SGD baselines are 89.83, 94.62, 94.52 on CIFAR-10 and 63.48, 76.88, 78.77 on CIFAR-100, ordered VGG11, ResNet34, DenseNet121. Adam values are 88.12, 94.30, 94.37 and 56.27, 72.81, 74.67. AdaBelief values are 91.24, 95.18, 95.44 and 67.59, 77.47, 79.20. Include the other adaptive comparators and reported standard deviations. These measure V4 even without quantified train/test gaps.
missing.locator: Table 9; Table 8; Section 4.1 hyperparameter tuning; Appendix E.1

missing.what: Recover the Adam-versus-SGD held-out perplexity ordering for each of the one-, two-, and three-layer Penn Treebank LSTMs. Both optimizers were run by this study, but their curves cannot be distinguished in the supplied text; SGDF's reported superiority does not determine their relative performance.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version. Do not use ImageNet Table 2's adaptive-versus-SGD numbers as independent results: those comparator values are cited from earlier work. SGDF-versus-SGD comparisons alone do not establish an Adam-type generalization disadvantage. No challenges label is warranted for adaptive-method wins because V4 already states a conditional, non-universal tendency.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or held-out performance comparison for random versus natural labels.
No width sweep or test-error behavior past zero training error.
No fully connected versus convolutional comparison or local-connectivity intervention.

The comparison concerns this paper's optimizer settings and benchmarks; it does not test the named studies' broader tuning regimes, optimizer switching, decoupled weight decay as a recovery mechanism, or word-level language-model exception.
No controlled large- versus small-batch comparison at fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout ablation or comparison with dropout and weight decay removed.
Hessian spectra, traces, and loss landscapes are reported, but no magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance measure is tested against train/test gaps or norm/margin measures.
No removal and retraining of memorized examples.

relationships.reason: From Table 9, absent from R1–R6: Adam and AdamW have lower mean best test accuracy than SGD in every combination; Adam's deficits range from 0.15 to 7.21 percentage points. This supports the optimizer ordering under the tested protocol, which includes additional tuning.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified comparisons place Adam below SGD throughout, while AdamW exceeds SGD on CIFAR-10 DenseNet121 and trails it elsewhere.
